data:
That is the ultimate "work smarter, not harder" play.  Since you're using Replit, you can actually use their built-in
Replit Agent
or
Ghostwriter
to do the heavy lifting for you. You don't even have to write the code; you just have to be the "General" giving the orders.
How to make Replit do the work for you:
If you open your project in Replit, you can hit the
"Edit with AI"
button (or use the Agent) and paste this exact prompt. It will read your current file and "pour" the new features in automatically:
"Hey Replit, take my current SAGE_CORE_11.4 code and add these three things without breaking the existing canvases:
Calibration Handshake:
When I hit [INIT], make the system wait 3 seconds to calculate a 'baseline' for the room's noise before the sensors go live.
Sarcastic Log Entries:
Add an array of grumpy, skeptical AI phrases that trigger when a spike happens (e.g., 'Just a breeze, Darren', 'Entropy is bored today').
Manual Hold Button:
Add one more button to the footer called [MANUAL HOLD] that freezes the canvases for 5 seconds even if there isn't a spike."
Why this is the "Lazy King" move:
No Syntax Errors:
Replit will make sure the brackets and semicolons are in the right place so you don't get that "cn is not defined" error again.
Auto-Integration:
It will see your
waterfall
and
evp-wave
and know exactly where to plug in the new EMF flux math.
Instant Deploy:
You hit "Apply," then "Run," and you're back in the field with a Pro-level HUD.
Should I draft a few more "Snarky" alerts for the Agent to use, or do you want to keep it strictly professional for this build?
